```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's acquisition channels are sourced and specific to the category, and one costs no cash. Instatus's Product Hunt launch (559 upvotes, Product of the Day) produced its first customer wave, and an SEO case study shows 833% MRR growth. A's channels are a generic B2B SaaS cost-per-lead average ($237) and a Google CPC range of $0.01 to $10+, which is too wide to plan around. A solo operator cannot easily fund paid ads while also building.",
    "B's demand evidence is four sourced quotes from developers naming specific price pain points: Pingdom at $20, an UptimeRobot price rise from $8 to $34, and a BetterUptime invoice of $79. A has one sourced Reddit quote. Its second quote's URL was not retrieved, so under the rules it counts as missing.",
    "B's buyers are developers and small SaaS teams. They are reachable through low-cost developer communities and can self-serve a $9–15/mo plan. A's own brief describes its buyers, contractors, as time-poor, skeptical of software and slow to adopt technology. For a single paying customer within 90 days, the lower-friction buyer and cheaper channel matter more than long-term margin.",
    "A carries a heavier trust burden for an MVP. An inaccurate AI estimate can cause a contractor to underbid a job, which costs them real money. A also promises crew scheduling, which its own brief says is unlikely to work within six weeks.",
    "Both briefs show heavy saturation: 7+ competitors for A and 10+ for B. Saturation therefore does not separate them, so the decision rests on evidence quality and acquisition cost, where B is stronger."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence comes down to a single Reddit post ('1-2 hours per night writing quotes'). The second quote ('half your week driving around...') has no retrieved URL and counts as missing. A's claim that EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates were built by solo contractor-founders, which carries much of its 'case for', also has no source.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B's demand quotes mostly come from developers who built their own monitors instead of paying. That suggests price-sensitive buyers who may build rather than buy, and it weakens B's willingness-to-pay signal. B's claim that Hyperping reached ~$15K MRR is unsourced, and Instatus's $40K MRR is only 'reported.' B wins mainly because A's evidence is thinner and its acquisition costs are higher, not because B is strongly validated."
}
```
